ip_top_stories.title: Historic NYT v. OpenAI copyright battle heats up
ip_top_stories.summary: The New York Times v. OpenAI case continues to advance as a landmark test of whether AI training on copyrighted material constitutes infringement. The case is widely watched as a potential precedent-setter for the entire AI industry's relationship with copyright holders.

ip_top_stories.title: DOJ Backs OpenAI In Landmark Copyright Fight Over AI Training And Fair Use
ip_top_stories.summary: The US Department of Justice has filed a brief supporting OpenAI's position in the NYT copyright case, arguing that AI training on copyrighted works may qualify as fair use. The move signals a significant federal policy stance favouring AI companies in copyright disputes.

ip_top_stories.title: Seattle Times and Newsday sue OpenAI and Microsoft over alleged copyright infringement
ip_top_stories.summary: Regional US newspapers Seattle Times and Newsday have filed a copyright lawsuit against OpenAI and Microsoft, alleging unauthorised use of their articles to train AI systems. The case adds to a growing wave of news publisher litigation against AI developers.

ip_top_stories.title: China's Supreme Court Sets the Rules for AI Liability — but Sidesteps the Biggest Copyright Question
ip_top_stories.summary: China's Supreme People's Court has issued its first national judicial guidelines on AI disputes, covering deepfakes and privacy, but has notably declined to rule on whether AI-generated works can be copyrighted. The guidelines set liability frameworks for AI providers while leaving the copyrightability question unresolved.

ip_top_stories.title: Operator of AI music generator can't escape copyright suit
ip_top_stories.summary: A US court has ruled that the operator of an AI music generator cannot have a copyright infringement suit dismissed, allowing the case to proceed. The ruling is significant for the AI-generated music sector and the broader question of liability for AI outputs that reproduce protected works.

ip_further_links.title: IP Hot Topic: The DOJ Chimes in on Fair Use and AI
ip_further_links.summary: Legal analysis of the DOJ's intervention in AI copyright cases and its implications for the fair use doctrine as applied to AI training data.

ip_further_links.title: Trump Admin Splinters Over AI's Right To Train On Your Copyrighted Work
ip_further_links.summary: Reporting reveals internal disagreements within the Trump administration over whether AI companies should have the right to train on copyrighted works without licence or payment.

ip_further_links.title: ANI appeals Delhi HC ruling that treated OpenAI's use of news for AI training as fair dealing
ip_further_links.summary: Indian news agency ANI has appealed to the Delhi High Court's Division Bench after a single judge denied interim relief, challenging the ruling that OpenAI's use of news content for AI training constituted fair dealing under Indian copyright law.

ip_further_links.title: AI Training & Copyright Part 3: Recent Case Law by the Regional Court of Munich (
ip_further_links.summary: Legal analysis of the Munich Regional Court's ruling in GEMA v. Suno, examining how German courts are applying copyright law to AI music generation and training data.

ip_further_links.title: China's 15th Five-Year Plan for Copyright Work Calls for AI Training Data and Generative AI Rules
ip_further_links.summary: China's new five-year copyright plan explicitly calls for the development of rules governing AI training data and generative AI, signalling a legislative push to regulate AI's relationship with intellectual property.

ip_further_links.title: Kenyan Tribunal Rules AI-Generated Works Need Human Input for Copyright
ip_further_links.summary: A Kenyan tribunal has ruled that AI-generated works require meaningful human creative input to qualify for copyright protection, aligning Kenya with similar positions taken in the US and elsewhere.

ip_further_links.title: India says AI cannot author a work, but it can still protect one
ip_further_links.summary: India has clarified its position on AI and copyright, stating that AI cannot be recognised as an author but that works with sufficient human creative input in their AI-assisted creation may still attract copyright protection.

ip_further_links.title: MinLaw and IPOS seek feedback on AI and Singapore's IP regime
ip_further_links.summary: Singapore's Ministry of Law and Intellectual Property Office have launched a public consultation on how AI should be addressed within Singapore's intellectual property framework, covering training data, authorship, and liability.

ip_further_links.title: Can Other Laws Stop AI-Imitated Painting Styles and Voices Beyond Copyright Law?
ip_further_links.summary: Analysis of whether existing laws beyond copyright — including personality rights, unfair competition, and trade dress — could be used to prevent AI systems from imitating artists' styles and voices.

ip_further_links.title: More papers target AI as tech, politics, and publishers draw battle lines
ip_further_links.summary: A growing number of news publishers are taking legal and political action against AI companies over the use of their content, with the article surveying the expanding landscape of publisher resistance.
